passes.scope: inclusion clauses 1-7 as written; lanes and queries declared before searching (docs/countries/QA_SYSTEMATIC_SWEEP.md); every published record reviewed blind by three independent roles and confirmed on its final text

lanes.source_family: QatarEnergy and QatarEnergy LNG: the LNG company's news archive and operator statements
registry: QatarEnergy LNG news archive; QatarEnergy statements
lanes.finding: Examined = 45 archive items + 2 report editions read + 2 events returned by the queries. The one item about a disruption is a February 2022 denial of press reports (rejected). The 2022 and 2023 reports give undated annual counts of process-safety events (four and five) and an undated remark tying a 2022 emissions rise to plant shutdowns, with no date, no planned or unplanned distinction and no production effect; these are not datable events and no candidate record was written for them.
lanes.limitation: The two force-majeure queries did not run (search cap). The operator's own newsroom is script-only, so its statements were seen only as press copies and search-result summaries. a facility's own sustainability reports (31-91 MB) and the LNG company's 2024 and 2025 reports were not read.

lanes.source_family: Electricity and water: utility and ministry statements carried by the state news agency
registry: KAHRAMAA and ministry statements (Qatar News Agency, Arabic and English)
lanes.finding: Examined = 107 utility news items (headlines) + 3 in-window press items opened. No dated power outage, blackout, emergency declaration or forced plant outage in Qatar for 2022-2026 was found, by the three queries or in the utility's own feed. The Arabic queries returned outages in other countries only. The English query returned the genre for earlier years: press copies of utility outage statements from 2013-2017, all outside the window, and none after. That amends the audit in two places: the utility's item pages are reachable by id, and it does publish reliability indices, though as percentages and through the press. Neither supplies an event. The correct reading remains low reported disruption, coverage unknown.
lanes.limitation: Three of six declared queries did not run (search cap), including both water-and-power queries, so no power-and-water plant outage was searched for at all. A query set is not a census of outages. The news agency could not be enumerated and none of its Qatar items surfaced in the results.

lanes.source_family: Arabic and English media by year, via search
registry: Domestic and international press (Al-Raya, Al-Sharq, Al-Watan, The Peninsula, Gulf Times, Al Jazeera, Reuters, S&P Global)
lanes.finding: The Arabic fire queries returned only English-language reports of the June explosion; Arabic reporting of it was not reached. Domestic Qatari outlets (QNA, Al-Raya, Al-Sharq, Al-Watan) appeared in results only as a QNA statement carried by Gulf Times and as QNA listing pages; international and regional outlets supplied the rest.
lanes.limitation: Seven of twenty declared strings were run, all Arabic; no English string and no 2026-tagged string was run, so the lane is partial in both language and year. The search engine ignored the year in every string and returned 2026 material each time, so the 2022-2025 strings say little about 2022-2025: finding nothing for those years is the result of seven queries and one newspaper category, not evidence that nothing happened. The Peninsula's Energy category is a thin, mostly oil-price listing (about 40 items a year) and carried none of the 2026 events, which the paper files elsewhere. Every article was read through a summarising fetch tool, not as raw text.
